root_cause: The _keydown method in tab.js uses getNextActiveElement which does not consider the disabled state of tabs, causing arrow navigation to move focus onto disabled tabs instead of skipping them.
repair_strategy: Replace the _keydown implementation with logic that iterates over the tablist children in the requested direction, skipping any disabled tabs, and wrapping to the start/end when needed, then activates the first enabled tab found.
expected_accessibility_effect: ArrowRight will skip the disabled Notifications tab and move focus to the Billing tab, updating aria-selected to true on Billing and showing its panel, while ArrowLeft will similarly skip disabled tabs in the reverse direction.
functional_risks: If all tabs are disabled, the logic may keep the current tab active (no change).
Vertical arrow keys (Up/Down) will also skip disabled tabs, which aligns with ARIA tablist behavior but could differ if upstream consumers relied on stopping at disabled tabs.
Change modifies the wrapping behavior when encountering consecutive disabled tabs at the edges.
verification_requirements: ArrowRight from Account tab moves focus to Billing tab and sets aria-selected=true on Billing.
ArrowLeft from Billing tab moves focus to Account tab and sets aria-selected=true on Account.
ArrowRight/Left never focus the disabled Notifications tab.
Tab panels show/hide correctly when activation occurs via arrow navigation.
Wrap‑around from last tab to first (and vice‑versa) still works when skipping disabled tabs.
